text:
Minnesota arrives with points in nine straight (7-0-2) and a 2-1 overtime win in Montreal two days ago, won by Kirill Kaprizov. Toronto is winless in four after a 6-3 home loss to Colorado, outscored 17-7 in that stretch, and the chances say it's real: just 42% of the expected goals. The Maple Leafs are also without Kirill Marchenko (lower body), who has 14 points in 14 games, though Morgan Rielly is day-to-day and could return.

Expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) favor the Wild at five on five, 53% to 46%. Minnesota's power play generates 0.92 expected goals a game against a Toronto penalty kill that allows 0.78, and the Leafs take 4.3 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt sits at +15.9 goals saved above expected this season (how many more goals he's stopped than the shots deserved), and is on a heater at .931 over his last five. Anthony Stolarz, projected for Toronto, is at +1.7 this year and -6.6 last season.

Kaprizov, the 135th pick in 2015, is on a nine-game point streak, and we have him at 49% to score. Matt Boldy sits at 41%. For Toronto, Jack Roslovic has 14 points in 10 games and has moved onto the first power-play unit with Marchenko out, while Auston Matthews is our top Leaf at 36%. Our under-the-radar pick is Minnesota's Bobby Brink, a third-liner with 2.9 expected goals in his last 10 games, 18% to score and 39% for a point.
